石琴為體鳴樂器，霍恩博斯特尔—薩克斯分類系統編號111.222。研究發現史前證據: The lithophone is an idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 111.222. Research has found prehistoric evidence: Sankarjang in Odisha, India, has an early stone-slab instrument, and studies of prehistoric stone tools in North America and Europe suggest possible portable lithophones. In 1785 Peter Crosthwaite described 'musical stones', sixteen stones arranged on a rope, with length and thickness deciding the pitch. The ancient Vietnamese lithophone đàn đá was revived in the twentieth century; in 1949 the Ndut Lieng Krak find yielded eleven slate slabs tuned to a pentatonic scale, now in the Museum of Mankind and possibly the oldest known instrument. The Korean pyeongyeong derives from the Chinese bianqing, and musical pillars are also found in Indian temples.
石琴的主要材質為天然岩石或礦物石料。樂器由多塊經過精心選擇的石頭組成，石頭的長度: The lithophone is made mainly of natural rock or mineral stone. The instrument consists of several carefully chosen stones, whose length, thickness and density determine their pitch. According to the historical account, Crosthwaite fixed the stones with rope so that they could hang or be supported in a particular position. Rocks of different hardness and composition, such as granite and slate, produce different timbres because of differences in density and elasticity. No wood, metal frame or leather is involved: the sound comes entirely from the physical properties of the stone.
石琴的聆聽示範可見於敲擊岩石板產生旋律或和聲的體鳴演奏，亦見於韓國儀式音樂中的石: Lithophones can be heard in idiophone playing that strikes stone slabs to produce melody or harmony, and also in the stone chimes of Korean ritual music, in the Basque traditional instrument the txalaparta, which can be made of stone, in the great stalactite organ of Luray Caverns in Virginia, USA, which plays Western scales on stalactites, and in Will Menter's sound sculptures and contemporary music. Carl Orff's later works use the stone lithophone Steinspiel; Wolfgang Lackerschmid's gramorimba and his trio with vibraphone and marimba; the Icelandic post-rock band Sigur Rós plays a slate marimba in the film Heima.
石琴音色清脆明亮，具有穿透力強的特徵，帶有質感堅實的金屬光澤。其音質乾淨透澈，敲: The lithophone has a clear, bright timbre that carries well, with the hard sheen of metal. Its tone is clean and transparent: a stroke gives a clear attack and then decays quickly. The range is wide, covering low, middle and high registers, though most instruments sit in the middle and upper register. It resonates by the natural resonance of the object itself, the rock vibrating directly, and the resonance lasts a comparatively short time. Next to the warm, heavy marimba the lithophone sounds colder and sharper; next to the xylophone it is more metallic and penetrating; but it is not as long and ringing as the glockenspiel. These qualities make it easy to pick out in an ensemble, and it is often used for a clear, spare texture.

A lithophone is an idiophone sounded by striking rock or stone slabs; it can play a melody note by note or in succession and can also combine notes in harmony. It is usually built of natural or trimmed stone slabs whose length and thickness determine the pitch, often hung or laid out as a scale. Hornbostel–Sachs classifies it as 111.222, directly struck percussion slabs. It is used in many places, from prehistoric remains and the stone chimes (pyeongyeong) of Korean ritual music to its use by modern composers and in sound installations.
站於琴前，雙手持棒敲擊琴鍵中央。手持樂器本體，透過敲擊、搖晃、刮奏或撥彈等方式使: Stand in front of the instrument and strike the middle of the bars with a beater in each hand. Hold the instrument itself and make it vibrate by striking, shaking, scraping or plucking. Different parts and different force give different timbres. In practising, first get the holding position right, then, once the basic way of sounding the instrument is secure, work on rhythm patterns and melody. Strike the surface with fingers or a beater and let the rebound carry the hand back naturally, keeping the wrist relaxed.
